title: 2021 Fall AMC 10B Problem 15
statement: In square \(ABCD,\) points \(P\) and \(Q\) lie on \(\overline{AD}\) and \(\overline{AB},\) respectively. Segments \(\overline{BP}\) and \(\overline{CQ}\) intersect at right angles at \(R,\) with \(BR = 6\) and \(PR = 7.\) What is the area of the square?

solutions.text:
Since \(BR=6\) and \(PR=7,\) we have \(BP=13.\) The right-angle and square-angle chasing gives \(\triangle PAB\cong\triangle QBC,\) so \(CQ=BP=13.\)

Because \(BP\perp CQ,\) point \(R\) is the foot of the altitude from \(B\) to the hypotenuse \(CQ\) of right triangle \(BQC.\) Thus \[QR\cdot RC=BR^2=36\] and \[QR+RC=CQ=13.\]

So \(QR\) and \(RC\) are \(4\) and \(9.\) Because \(P\) lies on \(\overline{AD},\) we have \(AP\le AB.\) Congruence gives \(BQ=AP,\) while the right-triangle projection formulas give \(BQ^2=CQ\cdot QR\) and \(BC^2=CQ\cdot RC.\) Hence \(QR\le RC,\) so \(QR=4\) and \(RC=9.\) Therefore, \[ \begin{aligned} BC^2&=BR^2+RC^2\\ &=6^2+9^2\\ &=117. \end{aligned} \]

The area of the square is \(117.\)

Thus, the answer is D .
hints: Use the altitude theorem in right triangle \(BQC\)
